newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL COFFEE EXPORTS IN SPIRIT OF ACPC PLAN-FEBEC.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL COFFEE EXPORTS IN SPIRIT OF ACPC PLAN-FEBEC.

text.p: Brazilian coffee exports in 1996/97 (July/June) were in keeping with the spirit of an agreement among key coffee producers which set export goals rather than quotas, a Brazilian coffee exporter official said.

"All the partners in the agreement of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) know that this export program is not a quota program," said Oswaldo Aranha, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Federation (Febec).

"The spirit of the agreement is of goals and all partners know the problems of countries such as Brazil in controlling their exports. In the spirit of the program, Brazil performed very well and tried its best to fulfill the program," he added.
Under the ACPC agreement, Brazil was to export 15 million 60-kg bags in the twelve months to end-June 1997. According to Febec statistics, actual shipments were 16.54 million.
Brazilian officials did however inform the ACPC secretariat in June that it was going to exceed its 15 million bag target.
Today Colombian coffee exporters launched a bitter attack on Brazil for its "flagrant violation" of export quotas.

In its bi-monthly publication, the Asoexport coffee exporters' association said that "when it comes to fulfilling promises and agreements, we don't know how many times our main partner Brazil will disappoint us."
Asoexport accused Brazil of taking advantage of soaring international prices earlier this year to sell as much coffee as it could.
But Aranha said Brazil could have sold a lot more coffee than it did.
"We definitely could have been a lot more aggressive than we were," he said.
Moreover the fact Brazil had substantially undershipped during a similar program in 1995/96 had not been the subject of comment, Aranha said.
"We didn't receive any comments when Brazil shipped a million bags less as happened last year," he said.
Top government coffee official Mauricio Assis from the Industry and Commerce Ministry was not immediately available to comment on the Asoexport remarks.
